headline: Chips drag Wall Street lower into the weekend, but oil holds its bid and stocks still log a winning week
tone: The softer PPI steadied the open, but the Nvidia hangover won the afternoon: the Nasdaq closed down 0.9%, the dollar stayed firm and money kept moving from renewables and metals into oil.
body: US stocks faded after the open. The S&P 500 closed down 0.4% at 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq down 0.9% at 25,136.27, while the Dow edged up 0.1% to 52,347.55. Chip stocks led the selling again as Nvidia fell for a sixth straight week after Jensen Huang's exit, with AMD and Broadcom the biggest drags. The S&P still finished the week up 2.5%, its first winning week since early October.
Europe closed flat: the STOXX 600 ended up 0.02% at 664.14, the DAX down 0.1%, the SMI down 0.3% and the FTSE 100 up 0.4%.
Oil kept a modest bid: Brent is up 0.4% at $96.16 and WTI up 0.2% at $88.92, though both are down about 2% on the week. Gas fell: TTF is down 2.9% at €89.55 and US gas down 2.8% at $3.25.

The dollar held its gains: EUR/USD is down 0.6% at 1.1025 and USD/CHF up 0.8% at 0.8391. The US 5-year is at 4.98% and the 30-year at 5.48%; our 10-year feed still shows Thursday's 5.10% close, up 12bp. The VIX rose 3.2% to 19.3.

views.text: Into oil, out of renewables and metals. TotalEnergies and Equinor are up 1.9%, Shell 1.5% and BP 1.4%, and the XLE energy ETF closed up 1.0%. Acciona Energía fell 6.9%, Orrön 6.0%, Grenergy 4.5% and Eolus 4.2%. Copper is down 2.2% and silver 2.7%, with copper miners (COPX) down 2.5%; gold is flat at $3,881.

The live gauge reads −10, which is mixed, down from +4 at the US open. The STOXX 600 5.4% above its 200-day average and the S&P 500 3.0% above still pull toward risk on. Thursday's 12bp jump in the US 10-year, a firmer dollar and copper lagging gold by 2.1% pull the other way, and only 6 of 14 indices are up.

views.section: What is priced in for next week
views.text: A Fed hike at the 8–9 December meeting stays fully priced after the PPI, with about a 10% chance of a half-point move (CME FedWatch). Next week brings Nvidia's results and the Anthropic IPO, both tests of appetite for AI stocks.
